All pings succeed with 0% loss. Network is fully repaired.

## Summary

### Errors found and fixes

**HQ (192.168.122.6)**
- `eth0` was `10.10.10.1/22`, should be `10.10.0.1/22` — corrected address.
- OSPF network was `10.10.0.0/21`, replaced with `10.10.0.0/22` to match eth0's subnet.
- No default-route redistribution — added `protocols ospf default-information originate always` so the static `0.0.0.0/0` reaches the branches.

**Branch1 (192.168.122.5)**
- No changes; configuration was already correct.

**Branch2 (192.168.122.7)**
- `eth2` (the WAN link to HQ) was administratively disabled — removed `interfaces ethernet eth2 disable`.
- `eth2` was marked OSPF passive while `eth0` wasn't — swapped so `eth0` (LAN) is passive and `eth2` participates in OSPF.
- OSPF network statement `10.10.4.0/22` didn't match any interface — replaced with `10.10.6.0/23` to cover eth0.
- Network `172.16.7.4/30` was already present, so eth2 joined OSPF once it came up.

### Verification results

OSPF neighbors (all Full):
- HQ: Branch1 via eth1, Branch2 via eth2 — 2 neighbors Full
- Branch1: HQ via eth1, Branch2 via eth2 — 2 neighbors Full
- Branch2: Branch1 via eth1, HQ via eth2 — 2 neighbors Full

Default route propagation: Branch1 and Branch2 both have `O>* 0.0.0.0/0` learned from HQ.

Routing tables: every router has OSPF routes to all remote LAN subnets (10.10.0.0/22, 10.10.4.0/23, 10.10.6.0/23) and all WAN /30s.

Ping tests (3/3 success, 0% loss on every test):
- HQ → PC1 (10.10.5.254) and PC3 (10.10.7.254): OK
- Branch1 → PC2 (10.10.3.254), PC3 (10.10.7.254), and 209.165.202.129: OK
- Branch2 → PC1 (10.10.5.254), PC2 (10.10.3.254), and 209.165.202.129: OK

All three routers were committed and saved.
